answer.verdict: DMA-tag QWC is added once in terminatePacketBuilderState, after the qword pad, as a whole-word addu of ((cur-tag)>>4)-1 when pk+8!=0. AddGsAD and CloseGifTag no longer write that word, so a later game-side ADD stores 2 and 5 instead of 4 and 10.

facts.c: refreshPacketBuilderPendingCount is gone. writePacketBuilderCurrent only writeGuestU32s cur. terminatePacketBuilderState pads while (cur&0xC), then if pk+8!=0 addu's ((cur-tag)>>4)-1 into the whole tag word via writeGuestBytes and clears pk+8.
ELF VIF terminate pads while (cur&0xC) before the addu (subu, sra 4, addiu -1, addu of the whole word, then pk+8=0). VIF Cnt stores an 8-byte CNT and sets cur=tag+8.
VIF Cnt then terminate therefore pads tag+8 to tag+16 and adds 0, so 0x10000000 stays 0x10000000. The 0x0FFFFFFF wrap is cur still on the tag (distance 0, add -1). Both passed.
Live test now expects low 16 == 0 before sceVif1PkTerminate and 0x10000001 with CNT id 0x10000000 after, then the one-qword GIF callback. Passed.
stub AddGsAD plus a game-side ADD close stores qwc once passed: VIF game close 0x10000002, GIF 0x10000005, stub terminate 0x10000002 once. Preloaded 0x10000003 plus one qword becomes 0x10000004.

contra: The design contra said a VIF Cnt close with cur=tag+8 adds -1 and yields 0x0FFFFFFF. ELF 0x292c18 and this terminate both pad first; tag+8 becomes tag+16 and the addu is 0, so the word stays 0x10000000 (test passed, log:781). 0x0FFFFFFF is the ELF result only when the post-pad distance is under 16 bytes (cur==tag). That path is implemented and passed (log:802). The old refresh also left the tag+8 shape at 0x10000000, because after the same pad deltaBytes==16 forced deltaQwords 0.
